CRM.rationale: CRM presents a compelling value case on operating metrics: Q1 FY2027 revenue of $11.13B grew +13.3% YoY, EPS surged +52.2% to $2.42, and operating cash flow was $6.70B. The PE has compressed to 18.7x from 54.5x a year ago — the floor of its 365-day range — with an implied PEG of ~0.36x on 52% EPS growth. Earnings yield of 5.3% now exceeds the 10Y Treasury at 4.57%. The franchise is dominant: 20% global CRM market share for 13 consecutive years, 150,000+ customers, 90%+ Fortune 500 penetration, and Agentforce ARR surpassing $1B (up 205%). However, the balance sheet has undergone a dramatic transformation — debt quintupled to $39.28B (D/E from 0.14x to 1.15x) likely tied to the Informatica acquisition, introducing material integration and leverage risk. Growth is also decelerating relative to peers (13% vs ServiceNow 22%, HubSpot 23%), and the market has not rewarded the strong Q1 print, suggesting skepticism about durability. The qualitative assessment is moderately positive — durable franchise at a compressed multiple facing identifiable but manageable transition risk. Near-term catalysts are limited: the IBM-driven software selloff (July 15) and mixed analyst actions (Evercore PT cut, KeyBanc downgrade offset by Guggenheim upgrade) create a neutral-to-slightly-negative near-term backdrop. Score reflects strong fundamentals and deep valuation discount partially offset by balance-sheet risk and growth deceleration vs peers.
